title: I Ching Hexagram Spectral Analysis
methodology: Same eigenvalue/SVD approach as yantra and magic cube explorations

findings.title: Fuxi arrangement is rank 2 — pure separability
findings.detail: The 8×8 Fuxi matrix (upper*8+lower) has rank 2, null 6. Almost all information in a single eigenvector. This is because Fuxi encoding is separable: f(u,l) = 8u + l decomposes as outer product of (0..7) with ones plus ones with (0..7). Maximally simple — pure combinatorial structure.

findings.title: King Wen arrangement is FULL RANK — maximally complex
findings.detail: The 8×8 King Wen matrix has rank 8, null 0. Every eigenvalue is nonzero and distinct. λ₂/λ₁ = 0.454, much higher than Lo Shu (0.327). King Wen is spectrally the opposite of Fuxi: maximum information distribution across all eigenvectors.
findings.note: Approximate mapping — 54/64 cells filled due to trigram assignment ambiguity

findings.title: Q₆ hypercube has BINOMIAL spectrum — Pascal's row 6
findings.detail: The 64×64 adjacency matrix of Q₆ (hexagrams connected if they differ by one line) has eigenvalues {6, 4, 2, 0, -2, -4, -6} = {6-2k} with multiplicities {1, 6, 15, 20, 15, 6, 1} = C(6,k). The I Ching's deep structure IS row 6 of Pascal's triangle.

findings.title: Balance matrix has 3 eigenvalues: {112, 16, 0}
findings.detail: The 64×64 matrix of shared yang lines (AND-popcount) has rank 6, with eigenvalues {112 (×1), 16 (×5), 0 (×58)}. 58 null dimensions. The yin-yang balance structure is extremely low-rank — only 6 independent balance modes.

findings.title: Hamming distance matrix: rank 7, eigenvalues {192, 0, -32}
findings.detail: The 64×64 Hamming distance matrix has only 3 unique eigenvalues. λ₁ = 192 = 3×64, λ₂ = 0 (×57), λ₃ = -32 (×6). The distance structure is even simpler than the adjacency structure.

findings.title: Complement permutation: eigenvalues exactly {+1, -1}
findings.detail: The complement operator (XOR with 63) is an involution — its only eigenvalues are ±1, each with multiplicity 32. The hexagram pairs form a perfect yin-yang partition of the 64-space.

findings.title: Structural comparison: Lo Shu vs Fuxi vs King Wen
findings.detail: Lo Shu: rank 3, concentrated spectrum (±2√6 universal), magic property. Fuxi: rank 2, trivially separable, no magic. King Wen: rank 8, maximally distributed spectrum, no magic. The Lo Shu occupies a unique middle ground — neither trivially separable nor maximally complex. Its magic property creates the ±2√6 invariant that has no analog in either I Ching arrangement.

synthesis.i_ching_deep_structure: The I Ching hexagram system is a 6D hypercube Q₆. Its spectral structure is the binomial distribution C(6,k) — Pascal's row 6. This is algebraically guaranteed by the hypercube graph structure, independent of any traditional ordering.
synthesis.fuxi_vs_king_wen: Fuxi = rank 2 (maximally ordered, separable). King Wen = rank 8 (maximally complex, full rank). They are spectral opposites — the two extremes of how to organize 64 hexagrams on an 8×8 grid.
synthesis.comparison_with_yantra: The Lo Shu/yantra system has a MAGIC property that creates universal spectral invariants (±2√6). Neither I Ching arrangement has this. The I Ching's invariant structure lives in the Q₆ hypercube adjacency, not in any matrix arrangement. Different systems, different spectral signatures.
